social_circle_metadata.note: Hattie is one year old, so personal messaging is realistically caregiver-mediated: these are the people most often texting with her household about Hattie, her care, visits, and family life.

social_circle.name: Tiana Moffett

demographics.occupation: primary caregiver; part-time home health aide
demographics.education: high school diploma with some community college coursework

background.how_they_met: Tiana is Hattie's mother and has cared for her since birth in Fayetteville.
background.why_close: She is Hattie's primary soothing attachment, knows her foods and routines best, and makes most day-to-day care decisions.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts in warm, direct full sentences, often with quick updates, photos, reminders, and occasional heart or laughing emoji.

shared_activities: naps and bedtime routines with music
quiet-room soothing when Hattie is overstimulated
recent_text_topics: Whether Hattie should have banana puree, avocado, or sweet potatoes when she refuses lumpy textures.
Planning quiet breaks after noisy family gatherings or church events.
Coordinating pediatric appointments, vaccine questions, diapers, and rides.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q05 says Hattie's mother knows her food preferences best and calms her fastest; Q11 says her mother handles breakfast and early care; Q41-Q42 say her mother has final say on vaccines guided by the pediatrician; Q44 says her mother took her to a quieter room, held her, and played gentle piano music.

social_circle.name: Marcus Moffett

background.how_they_met: Marcus is Hattie's father and has lived with her since birth.
background.why_close: He is part of her core household, helps with evening care, plays with her, and shares family downtime such as baseball games.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Short, casual texts with jokes, sports references, quick check-ins, and photo reactions.

shared_activities: block play and crawling around the living room
recent_text_topics: Joking that Hattie is already a Red Sox fan because she claps at crowd noise.
Checking whether Hattie napped before dinner and whether she is too tired for visitors.
Coordinating diapers, groceries, transportation, and family visits.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q05 says Hattie's father watches baseball with her and jokes that she is already a Boston Red Sox fan; Q11 says she lives with her mother and father; Q106 says his role includes care, play, family time, and sharing sports watching.

social_circle.name: Denise McNeill

demographics.occupation: school cafeteria worker and church volunteer

background.how_they_met: Denise is Hattie's grandmother and has been present throughout Hattie's first year.
background.why_close: She visits often, helps with childcare, sings to soothe Hattie, and is one of the first relatives the family asks for help.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts with affectionate greetings, prayerful language, practical reminders, and voice notes when singing or checking in.

shared_activities: singing gospel or soft songs to calm Hattie
helping with childcare during tight schedules
recent_text_topics: Offering to come by when Hattie is fussy, sick, or overstimulated.
Asking whether the family needs diapers, baby clothes, or a ride.
Sending prayers and checking how Hattie slept after noisy visits.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q05 says Hattie's grandmother sings to her and calms her after her mother; Q11 says grandmother is present often enough that Hattie treats her as part of daily life; Q35 says grandmother would be hardest to lose help from; Q46 says grandmother supports the family.

social_circle.name: Keisha Moffett

background.how_they_met: Keisha is one of Hattie's nearby aunties in the Fayetteville/Hoke County family network.
background.why_close: She visits often, helps with childcare or supplies, and is trusted because Hattie recognizes her voice and warms up when visits are calm.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts in practical bursts, often confirming plans, offering help, and sending quick health or baby-care suggestions.

shared_activities: bringing hand-me-down clothes or baby supplies
recent_text_topics: Whether Keisha can stop by so Tiana can run errands or rest.
Hand-me-down clothes as Hattie grows into larger sizes.
Reminders to keep Hattie's routine calm around loud cousins or busy gatherings.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q01 says Hattie's main people include aunties; Q06 says nearby aunties and uncles are part of the immediate family and an auntie visits most; Q13 says an auntie may visit weekly or when childcare help is needed; Q79 says grandmother and aunties help with childcare.

social_circle.name: Monique Carter

demographics.occupation: childcare assistant at a community center
demographics.education: associate degree in early childhood education

background.how_they_met: Monique knows Hattie's family through their Black church community and local child-centered activities.
background.why_close: She is a trusted non-household adult who checks on the baby, shares parenting advice, and is part of the family's church support network.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Friendly and upbeat, with full-sentence texts, church phrases, reminders, and occasional voice messages.

recent_text_topics: Community center swim times and toddler-friendly events.
Checking whether Hattie handled church noise, clapping, and familiar faces well.
Offering prayer, parenting tips, and suggestions for calm sensory routines.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q07 identifies church friends, toddler gym caregivers, and community center swim staff as important outside-family adults; Q47 says church is both spiritual support and a practical network where people ask about the baby and offer advice; Q49 says family may use messaging to ask for prayer, advice, or baby supplies.
